header.lede: Every id-stable interface works — until trees get big or sessions get long. Then only anchored patches do, and they barely need to see the tree. Finding where to look costs one search call, and remembering the session costs two worked examples plus a memo — even 36 edits in. And the view is a correctness contract: what the model must read, it must be shown. Views carry values; memos carry goals — the agent can be trusted to write the memo itself, and "undo that" needs an echo, not a transcript. The standing brand pack simply works — and when a rule collides with a request, models pick a reading rather than break either; our first claim about WHICH reading was refuted by its own confirmation study a day later. And the series-long villain fell last: offered one sentence of permission, every model asked instead of guessing, 270/270 — the silence was protocol, not blindness. Then the whole core stack was re-run on the tier the downstream surfaces actually ship, claude-opus-4.8, and every gate passed: the frontier does not need the training wheels, though they cost nothing to keep. And when we probed the ask path for its breaking point, the tax was zero and the answer loop was perfect; the one crack is that below the frontier tier, models silently resolve ambiguous references instead of asking about them. And the one clause we had shipped on faith got its audit: making the model restate a goal it read does nothing, because where a goal comes from matters more than whether the model says it aloud. And the memo passed its stress test everywhere but one place: filled to its twenty-note cap, it silently throws away exactly the thing it exists to remember. Then we measured the obvious fix for the ambiguity gap, and it rescued the model we do not run while adding nothing to the one we do; some gaps are capabilities, not prompts. The last border closed with fine print: the ask sentence covers dangling references on every tier, and its zero tax turns out to presume the very view contract it rides along with. And the oldest habit in the protocol got its control group at last: told nothing but "that was invalid," the models fixed their patches anyway. The error message was for us, not them.
header.provenance: Main study: 200 seeded tasks × 6 conditions × 4 models × 2 regimes, temperature 0 (July 2026), plus follow-up studies G (tool-history footgun), H (300–1000-node size extension), I/J (focused views: partial-context patches, JSON and HTML renderings), K (12-edit sessions under four serialization policies), L/N (grounding without ids, then the retrieval ladder), M/O/P (session memory, positional views, synthetic history), Q/R (fan-out edits and their fixes), S (36-edit long sessions), T (conversation-carried context), U (document-carried dependencies), V (qualitative rewrites — the series' first judge-graded study, disclosed as its own track), W (agent-maintained memo extraction, the shipped mechanism verbatim, with claude-opus-4.8 as a third tier), X (edit-anaphora: amend, repeat, and undo follow-ups racing four context carriers), and Y (naturalistic extraction: twin sessions isolating declaration phrasing, with chatter bait for the noise metric). All numbers below are protocol-v2 corrected — the original interface-reliability gaps were an artifact of conversation histories that hid the model's own tool calls (vercel/ai#16840). Charts show parity prompts, models pooled unless noted; Wilson 95% intervals. Conditions: A HTML + whole-tree rewrite, B JSON + rewrite, C JSON + mutation tools, D HTML + tools, E JSON Patch, F id-anchored patch (pre-registered addendum, BRIEF-F.md), and AD (the Opus confirmation: the core stack re-run verbatim on claude-opus-4.8, 1,160 cells), and AE (the calibration ladder: five ambiguity levels plus the ask-answer-resume loop, 720 cells), and AF (restate-before-rewrite, judge-graded: 270 contemporaneous edits, both judges re-calibrated 100/100), and AH (memo saturation: recall, rules, and full-replace integrity at the shipped 20-note cap, 270 cells), and AI (the multiplicity hatch: the amended ask sentence vs the shipped one across the full ladder, 450 cells), and AG (the anaphora hatch: the shipped ask sentence on the undo-that construction plus the echo-tax co-check, 1,296 session steps), and AJ (the correction loop in isolation: seeded failures, structured vs codes vs bare feedback, 405 cells), and AK (eviction validation: the goal-preserving eviction re-measured at the Study AH injury site, 120 cells), and AL (the prompt-side fence: an anti-self-eviction sentence vs the AK-eviction arm as contemporaneous control, the prompt rule the only variable, 120 cells), and AM (consolidation-on-notice: an invitation appended to the app's eviction notice, the notice string the only variable, on a fresh 40-task cap-edge corpus, 240 cells), and AN (ask or act: the visibility-clause tax re-measured with a view tool in hand — tool availability alone dissolves it on every tier, while the tested fetch-before-ask clause proves redundant on the frontier and unsafe below it, 1,728 session steps), and AO (canonical-tag steering: does advisory lint keep agent-written tags on an org's catalog — the catalog-read tool proves to be the whole mechanism, consulted unprompted in every cell, while unguided models drift 36/36 and lint-only arms cannot recover, 324 cells).

asks on provably-unsolvable edits once a one-sentence escape hatch existed — against 0/270 silent wrong patches without it, with zero false asks on the solvable twins (Study AC)

sections.eyebrow: H2 · task success by tree size
sections.title: At benchmark sizes (5–150 nodes), no interface dominates
sections.takeaway: Whole-tree rewrite (A, B) leads granular tools (C, D) at every size tested. The gap peaks on small/medium trees and narrows — but never reverses — at ~150 nodes. JSON Patch (E) collapses to 69.6% on large trees — and the pre-registered addendum condition F (id-anchored patches) recovers it exactly to rewrite level at the lowest token cost.

sections.title: Corrected: multi-turn reference edits are near-parity
sections.takeaway: Success on “insert a node, then edit it by the id from your own output” — protocol v2. With the model's own tool history visible, every interface is near-parity (A 88.1% vs C 91.3%, n.s.); gemini's residual tools deficit is phase-1 editing accuracy, not follow-up dropout. Zero id-reference failures in any arm, ever. The dramatic v1 gaps live in the footgun chart below.

sections.eyebrow: H3 · mean tokens per solved task
sections.title: Rewrite is cheap where trees are small; HTML is the terser artifact where they're large
sections.takeaway: Tools arms (C, D) resend a growing conversation every call, so they burn 4–5× more tokens on small/medium trees. At ~150 nodes the whole-artifact arms grow too — and the HTML dialect (A, 15.6k) undercuts JSON rewrite (B, 23.0k) by ~30%: the one place the format measurably matters.
